analyst_view.overall: Nordsjaelland (25th, 2 pts) host Panathinaikos (2nd, 9 pts from three wins): the Danes need a win to climb into the top 24, while Panathinaikos, on five straight wins in all competitions, would move close to a top-eight place. Nordsjaelland beat Copenhagen 5-0 and Randers 6-1 in their last two league games, form the numbers only partly see, though they have not won their last three home games in Europe on their artificial pitch. Panathinaikos, under Jacob Neestrup, are without Andino, Ounahi and Ingason (counted) and flew to Denmark on Wednesday without centre-back Stefan de Vrij (wrist) and left-back Giorgos Kyriakopoulos (muscle), neither of whom the numbers know about; Christiansen travels as the only natural left-back, and Salah-Eddine is not registered for Europe. Austrian referee Julian Weinberger is named, and the numbers already add about 10% to cards for his record.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, split 1.5 to 1.2, already taking off Andino, Ounahi and Ingason for Panathinaikos. De Vrij and Kyriakopoulos are confirmed out of the travelling squad by several Greek outlets, leaving Palmer-Brown or Katris in the middle and the untested Christiansen at left-back, which the numbers can't see, and Nordsjaelland have scored eleven in their last two league games. I keep +6%, about 2.9 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, split evenly. Both sides like the ball and the numbers already reflect their corner records; losing Kyriakopoulos takes some crossing from the left for Panathinaikos while Nordsjaelland may attack more down that side, which roughly cancels, so I stay at about 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards, already raised about 10% for Panathinaikos' recent bookings and 10% for referee Weinberger's record (5.2 a game). A reshuffled Panathinaikos back line may have to foul more against Nordsjaelland's quick attack, but that is a guess on top of an already high figure, so I stay at about 5.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots, already raised 5% for Nordsjaelland's recent volume. Nordsjaelland's home attack should push that up, but a Panathinaikos side keeping the ball on an artificial surface can slow the game, so I stay at about 26.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target, already nudged up for both sides' recent accuracy. Nordsjaelland's sharp league finishing and a Panathinaikos defence confirmed without de Vrij and Kyriakopoulos, neither of which the numbers can see, point slightly higher: +4% gives about 10.0.
